user.title: Load Need Predictor
user.description: Set when to predict (after tomorrow's prices publish) and when to capture the day's actual delivery.

data_description.predict_time: Time of day to compute the prediction and push it to the scheduler target — set it just after tomorrow's day-ahead prices publish.
data_description.capture_time: Time of day to record the actual delivered energy — the day ending at this time — as a training sample (typically end of day).

data_description.predict_time: Time of day to compute the prediction and push it to the scheduler target — set it just after tomorrow's day-ahead prices publish.
data_description.capture_time: Time of day to record the actual delivered energy — the day ending at this time — as a training sample (typically end of day).

init.title: Load
init.description: Pick the scheduler target, delivery and occupancy sources, and runtime clamp. Temperature sources are log-only. Optional tank tracking estimates stored heat; shower sources record observations without changing heating control.

data.name: Name
data.appliance_household_activity_entities: Household activity near water uses (optional, appliance observations)

data_description.target_number_entity: The Load Scheduler target number this predictor drives (e.g. number.water_heater_lvv_target_runtime). The prediction is written here.
data_description.delivered_energy_entity: Energy delivered to the load (kWh, total/increasing). Its day-to-day change is the training signal.
data_description.delivered_runtime_entity: Optional run-time sensor; used as the delivered signal instead of energy ÷ rated power when run-time is the better measure.
data_description.controlled_switch_entity: The load's switch/contactor — the relay the scheduler drives. Its recorded on-time (from any source: scheduler, a manual boost, an automation) measures the runtime actually delivered, so a day the scheduler skips on price/solar is carried over and made up the next day. Pick the real contactor, not a thermostat-gated power sensor. Leave empty to disable catch-up.
data_description.rated_power_kw: The load's power draw, used to convert predicted energy (kWh) into a run-time (minutes) for the scheduler target.
data_description.person_entities: People whose presence shifts demand. Counted when home for at least 12 h of the last 24 h, so a daytime absence (e.g. a meeting) doesn't drop them.
data_description.guests_calendar_entity: Calendar marking guest visits. Demand is weighted by visit length — a short visit (< 6 h) counts as ~half a person, a long one (≥ 6 h, likely sauna + showers) as two.
data_description.supply_temp_entity: Incoming mains-water temperature. Logged for a future model; not used in the current prediction.
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: Outdoor temperature. Logged for a future model; not used in the current prediction.
data_description.water_total_entity: Cumulative household water meter. Logged as day-ahead context; tank tracking also uses its deltas for the energy balance and optional shadow observations.
data_description.heating_active_entity: Binary sensor that is on only while the element actually draws power (contactor AND internal thermostat, e.g. an LED or current detector). Together with the controlled switch it detects a thermostat trip while commanded on and anchors the stored-heat estimate. This does not measure outlet temperature or guarantee shower comfort. Leave empty to disable tank tracking.
data_description.tank_cold_in_c: Cold-water inlet temperature at the house (annual average). Used to compute the tank's energy capacity.
data_description.tank_boost_soc_pct: When the calibrated tank charge falls below this percentage, re-run predict + push immediately so the scheduler plans more heating. Leave empty to disable.
data_description.min_minutes: Lower clamp on the pushed target — a safety floor so the load never starves.
data_description.max_minutes: Upper clamp on the pushed target — a cap so a bad prediction can't over-run the load.
data_description.deficit_cap_minutes: Largest backlog the catch-up can accumulate (minutes). Defaults to twice the daily cap — enough to recover a couple of skipped days without runaway after a long outage. Only used when a controlled switch is set.
data_description.shower_motion_entity: Binary occupancy/motion sensor near the shower. Used with water and humidity to identify possible shower events; motion alone is not proof of a shower.
data_description.shower_humidity_entity: Bathroom relative-humidity sensor. Humidity rise adds evidence to a shower event; missing readings remain unknown.
data_description.shower_ventilation_entity: Binary sensor or input boolean indicating a shower-triggered ventilation boost. Supplemental evidence only; automatic ventilation alone does not confirm a shower.
data_description.cold_appliance_entities: Running/status entities for cold-fed appliances such as a dishwasher or washing machine. Use actual running signals, not overall appliance availability. An unavailable appliance counts as powered off (cloud appliances drop offline when switched off) unless it dropped offline mid-run; unknown or unrecognised states remain unknown. Used only in the shadow observation log.
data_description.shower_target_temp_c: Preferred shower temperature (30–45 °C, default 40 °C) for observation context. This does not change the tank thermostat or heating target.
data_description.appliance_household_activity_entities: Motion or occupancy sources near other water uses (bathroom, toilet, shower). Activity flags possible household overlap; no activity does not prove all water belongs to an appliance. Empty or unavailable sources remain unknown. Shadow analysis only.

error.invalid_runtime_band: No whole 15-minute step fits between the minimum and maximum minutes/day (e.g. min 40 / max 40). Widen the range so it contains at least one multiple of 15 (e.g. 45).
error.heating_needs_switch: The heating-active detector needs the controlled switch too: the tank charge is calibrated at 'contactor on + element idle', which can't be seen without the switch.
error.invalid_shower_temperature: Preferred shower temperature must be between 30 and 45 °C.

init.title: Beyond-horizon price forecast
init.description: Forecast electricity prices beyond Nord Pool's day-ahead horizon at 15-minute resolution and publish them for the scheduler's forecast_price_entity. The primary source is the free Wattcast forecast (wattcast.eu — prices: Elering/Nord Pool, weather: Open-Meteo), converted to your all-in price with a mapping learned from your real prices. A local wind + temperature model fills in beyond Wattcast's coverage or when it is unreachable.

data.name: Name
data.price_series_entity: Real price series sensor (optional, e.g. Nord Pool day-ahead)
data.weather_entity: Weather entity (daily temperature forecast, local fallback)
data.temp_history_entity: Outdoor temperature sensor (for fitting the local fallback)

data_description.price_entity: Your real all-in buy-price sensor (€/kWh). The local model is fit on its history and every forecast source is evaluated against it.
data_description.price_series_entity: A sensor whose attributes carry the real price slots (data_yesterday / data_today / data_tomorrow with start + buy, like the Load Scheduler's buy-price entity). Used to learn the spot → all-in price mapping (VAT, margin, transfer tariff) and to know where real prices end. Without it the mapping learns slowly from the buy-price sensor's current value.
data_description.use_wattcast: Fetch the Wattcast spot-price forecast (about 7 days, 15-min, with a p10–p90 band) once an hour. Results are cached, survive restarts, and are kept until a newer forecast arrives.
data_description.wattcast_zone: Nord Pool bidding zone to forecast.
data_description.vat_pct: VAT applied to the spot price. Only seeds the mapping until enough real prices have been paired with Wattcast's settled spot.
data_description.wind_entity: Finland wind-production forecast sensor — more wind generally means lower prices. Only used by the local fallback model.
data_description.weather_entity: Weather entity providing the daily temperature forecast — colder means higher prices. Only used by the local fallback model.
data_description.temp_history_entity: Outdoor temperature sensor whose recorded history is used to fit the local fallback model.
data_description.forecast_days: How many days after today to publish (Wattcast covers about 7; the local model fills any remainder).
data_description.fit_days: How many days of history to fit the local price model on.

configured_source_unhealthy.title: Configured source unavailable for {load}
configured_source_unhealthy.description: The configured source {source} for {load} has a persistent problem: {problem}. Reconfigure this load in Settings → Devices & services → Load Need Predictor to select the correct source, or restore the source integration. Unknown readings remain uncertain; a replacement sensor is not selected automatically. This issue clears when the source recovers or its configuration is changed.

wattcast_unreachable.title: Wattcast price forecast unreachable
wattcast_unreachable.description: The Wattcast price forecast for zone {zone} could not be fetched for more than {hours} hours (last success: {last_success}; last error: {error}). The last cached forecast is still being used while it lasts, and the local model fills the rest. This clears automatically once a fetch succeeds.

report_shower_comfort.name: Report shower comfort
report_shower_comfort.description: Attach a comfort observation to a retained shower event. This does not change stored heat, heating or scheduler targets.

event_id.name: Shower event
event_id.description: Event ID from the estimated stored heat sensor's recent_showers attribute.

comfort.name: Comfort
comfort.description: How warm the selected shower felt.
